assumptions: The data dictionary is authoritative for the semantics of feature, future_score, mass_value, and target_copy.
An exact duplicate means equality across every CSV column; this definition identifies the second occurrence of row_id 5.
Dates are ISO-8601 calendar dates and may be sorted lexicographically.
The proposed conversion 1 tonne = 1000 kg is a standard unit identity; it makes row_id 3 equal to 12 kg, but the raw value remains unchanged.
R is likely an alias of red, but that normalization is not treated as verified because the local dictionary supplies no category map.

baseline.description: No predictive baseline was run because the requested work is an audit and the 10 unique records are insufficient for a credible standalone performance estimate.
evidence: The audit verified 11 raw rows and 10 unique full rows.
No command trained a model or calculated a model metric.

claims: Verified evidence supports exact duplication, invalid negative mass, one missing feature, mixed units, a documented sentinel, a documented plausible bulk value, nonchronological file order, and two leakage columns.
The proposed entity-disjoint outer evaluation prevents the same entity from appearing in both train and held-out data.
Excluding future_score and target_copy before preprocessing prevents the two verified direct leakage paths identified in the local data.
The audit is complete for the supplied local evidence; model quality and production temporal generalization remain untested.

data_findings: Verified error: row_id 5 occurs twice as an exact full-row duplicate; deduplicate only in a derived analysis view and retain the immutable raw rows plus a removal log.
Verified error: row_id 4 has mass_value -5 kg, an invalid negative amount; quarantine it from modeling until corrected or explicitly excluded, without guessing a replacement.
Verified missingness: row_id 3 has the sole empty feature value; any imputation must be fitted on training data only and accompanied by a missingness indicator.
Verified category inconsistency: raw labels are red, Red, R, blue, BLUE, and green. Case normalization is justified for Red/red and BLUE/blue; mapping R to red remains a human-gated proposal.

Verified mixed units, not intrinsically an error: row_id 3 uses 0.012 tonne while all other raw rows use kg; a derived canonical-mass field may convert it to 12 kg while preserving the original value and unit.
Verified plausible extreme, not an error: row_id 9 has 250 kg, and the dictionary explicitly states that bulk shipments up to 300 kg are possible.

Verified sentinel, not an ordinary numeric extreme or missing value: row_id 8 has feature 99, which the dictionary identifies as a known device-mode sentinel; encode a sentinel indicator and do not use 99 as a continuous measurement.
Verified ordering issue, not a proven bad date: entity A appears in file order 2026-01-01, 2026-01-03, 2026-01-02; sort within entity by date before temporal feature construction.
Verified direct leakage: target_copy equals target in all 11 raw rows and is documented as derived from target; exclude it from every predictor set and preprocessing fit.
Verified future leakage: future_score is recorded one day after target and equals target plus 1 in all 11 raw rows; exclude it from predictors for target-time prediction.
The absent row_id 6 is only an identifier gap; local evidence does not establish that a record is missing, so it is not classified as a data error.
row_id is an identifier rather than a substantive predictor and must be excluded from modeling.
experiment_design: Create a derived analysis view: retain the raw files, log and remove only exact duplicate row occurrences, normalize mass into a separate kilogram field, preserve original unit fields, and quarantine the negative-mass row.
Exclude row_id, future_score, and target_copy before any feature inspection, preprocessing, or fit.
Use six outer leave-one-entity-out folds so no entity appears in both training and held-out data.
Within each outer-training set, fit all data-dependent preprocessing only on training rows; apply frozen transformations to the held-out entity.
Treat feature 99 via a device-mode indicator rather than as a continuous measurement; add a separate indicator for the genuinely missing feature.
Sort each entity by date before any lag construction and require every feature for a prediction date to be available no later than that date.
If tuning is unavoidable, nest entity-grouped validation entirely inside the outer-training partition; otherwise pre-specify the model to avoid unstable tuning on this sample.
Store fold assignment, raw-row lineage, exclusion reasons, transformation parameters, input hashes, and fold-level predictions in the audit record.
falsification_tests: Assert no entity intersects between train and held-out partitions in any outer fold.
Assert row_id, future_score, and target_copy are absent from every fitted pipeline input and serialized feature list.
Shuffle target_copy and future_score or remove them entirely; eligible-feature predictions must remain identical because those columns are excluded upstream.
Assert each retained derived row maps to a raw row and that exactly one occurrence of the duplicated full row is excluded with an explicit reason.
Assert no feature timestamp exceeds its prediction timestamp after within-entity sorting and lag construction.
Fit preprocessing independently per fold and compare stored training statistics with held-out statistics to detect accidental whole-data fitting.

constraints: All copies of one entity must remain in one outer fold.
Exact-row deduplication must occur before fold assignment using a logged derived view, never by changing raw data.
future_score, target_copy, and row_id must never enter features or preprocessing.
Category mapping, missing-value handling, sentinel encoding, scaling, and fitting must be learned or configured without inspecting held-out outcomes.
The negative-mass record remains quarantined unless a human-authorized correction rule is supplied.
Within-entity records must be date-sorted before constructing any lagged or historical feature; no future observation may inform an earlier prediction.
notes: With six entities, leave-one-entity-out evaluation maximizes use of this tiny dataset while blocking entity overlap.
If hyperparameters are tuned, use an inner entity-grouped split on outer-training entities only; report fold-level predictions and uncertainty rather than relying on a single aggregate score.
A production temporal claim would require more entities and longer histories; this split design alone cannot create that evidence.
formalization.objective: Estimate out-of-entity predictive performance for target without using post-target, target-derived, identifier, duplicate, quarantined-invalid, or test-fitted information.
parameters: Outer evaluation has six leave-one-entity-out folds, one per distinct entity.
Canonical mass conversion parameter: 1 tonne = 1000 kg.
units: mass_value is paired with mass_unit; proposed derived canonical mass is kilograms.
target, feature, and future_score have no units specified in the local dictionary.
variables: Eligible contemporaneous predictors after audit: normalized category, canonical mass plus original-unit provenance, and audited feature value with missing/sentinel indicators.

human_gates: Confirm or reject the proposed R-to-red category mapping before using that row in a normalized categorical feature.
Provide an authoritative correction or exclusion decision for row_id 4; no correction was invented.
Confirm which contemporaneous fields are operationally available at target prediction time before modeling.
No human approval was received or inferred during this run.
reality_constraints: The raw CSV has 11 rows, only 10 unique full rows, six entities, and very limited temporal depth.
Only entities A, B, and C have repeated raw observations; after exact deduplication their counts are 3, 2, and 2 respectively, while D, E, and F have one each.
No external source, network access, MCP, remote, credential, parent directory, or historical material was used.
No model was trained and no predictive metric was computed; this run is a data audit and split design.
Raw inputs were not edited; derived records are stored under case/output.
requirements: Inspect only the listed local inputs in the isolated repository and preserve them unchanged.
Audit injected data issues, distinguishing errors from plausible extremes and unsupported inferences.
Design a leakage-safe split and a structured, recoverable audit record.
Return exactly one observation object conforming to observation.schema.json without inventing evidence or approval.
robustness_tests: Report fold-level results and repeat aggregate summaries with each singleton held-out entity omitted in turn to expose sensitivity to D, E, or F.
Compare a primary analysis that quarantines row_id 4 with a labeled sensitivity analysis that excludes all mass features; do not silently impute the negative mass.
Compare analyses with R quarantined versus human-confirmed R-to-red mapping.
Verify invariance to raw CSV row order by rerunning the derived pipeline after permutation while retaining explicit date sorting.
Verify that treating row_id 9 as valid rather than deleting it is documented; optionally report a sensitivity analysis without mass predictors, not an unsupported outlier deletion.
